Let $G$ be a connected reductive group, $P$ a parabolic subgroup of $G$, and $S$ a subset of $G$ with the restrictions that the paper imposes on $S$ in its standing notation; these restrictions are not stated in the given context and are left as in the paper. Let $G^S$ be the centralizer of $S$ in $G$, $(G^S)^o$ its identity component, and $B^S\subset (G^S)^o$ a Borel subgroup. Let $X_P^S$ be the smooth variety of the paper, and let $W^P$ be the set of minimal length representatives of the cosets $W/W_P$. Let
\[
Y_S:=\{v\in W^P:\ B^S\cdot vP/P=vP/P\}.
\]
Then the connected components of $X_P^S$ are in bijection with $Y_S$. For $v\in Y_S$ let $X_P^S(v)$ be the connected component corresponding to $v$. The morphism $\hat\phi_v:(G^S)^o\to X_P^S$, $g\mapsto g\cdot vP/P$, descends to a $(G^S)^o$-equivariant isomorphism of varieties
\[
\phi_v:(G^S)^o/\bigl((G^S)^o\cap vPv^{-1}\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim} X_P^S(v).
\]
Moreover $B^S\subset (G^S)^o\cap vPv^{-1}$ for every $v\in Y_S$, and since $X_P^S$ is smooth, its connected components coincide with its irreducible components.

The variety X_P^S is not defined in the given context; it is read as the smooth variety of the paper.
